title: The rise of retro fashion
paragraphs: Do you take care about what you wear? Some people are very fashion-conscious, carefully selecting the clothes they buy and how they dress. Fashionistas always want to be seen in the latest designer gear. But that trend is changing as retro or vintage clothing is becoming a popular and often cheaper alternative.

Of course, ‘vintage’ clothing is really second-hand clothing, worn before but given a new lease of life. The fashion industry has rebranded this stuff to make it look trendy and possibly give it a higher price tag. Whereas we may have seen an old faded pair of jeans or a gingham-patterned dress sold at a jumble sale, now there are boutique and pop-up shops dedicated to the stuff. And in the UK, one supermarket chain has started selling second-hand clothes in some of its stores under the brand, Preloved Vintage Wholesale. Its managing director Steve Lynam told the BBC: "The more people that buy into the circular economy and shop vintage and retro, the bigger impact we will have on climate change."

Certainly, buying vintage does prolong the life of clothing. It cuts down on waste and helps to reduce the environmental damage caused by manufacturing new clothes. It’s also led to the rise of retro-fashion – items that your mum or dad wore decades ago that now look ‘cool’ again! It’s a big thing with younger people and has been helped by the rise of platforms like Depop and Vinted, which sell ‘worn’ clothes online. Ianina Lucca from Depop told the BBC: “The new generation is… looking to make choices that reduce their impact on the environment, with 77% of Gen Z saying that their biggest environmental concern being that they want their choices to reduce waste.”

Another popular way of buying old clothes is in a vintage kilo sale. People pick what they want and then pay according to weight rather than per item. Some items are upcycled – re-modelled or re-worked by adding embroidery, patches and other additions. But however these second-hand clothes are worn or re-designed, the sustainability of vintage fashion means it’s here to stay for some time to come.

vocabulary.entry: fashion-conscious /ˈfæʃn ˈkɒnʃəs/ adj. 注重时尚的；赶时髦的
vocabulary.example: She has always been fashion-conscious, even when she was a teenager.
vocabulary.translation: 她从青少年时期起就一直很注重时尚。

vocabulary.entry: fashionista /ˌfæʃnˈiːstə/ n. 时尚达人；追随时尚的人
vocabulary.example: The party was full of fashionistas showing off their latest outfits.
vocabulary.translation: 聚会上满是炫耀最新穿搭的时尚达人。

vocabulary.entry: designer gear /dɪˈzaɪnə ɡɪə/ n. 设计师品牌服饰
vocabulary.example: She saved up for months to buy that piece of expensive designer gear.
vocabulary.translation: 她攒了好几个月的钱才买下那件昂贵的设计师品牌服饰。

vocabulary.entry: retro /ˈretrəʊ/ adj. 复古的；怀旧的
vocabulary.example: The café is decorated in a retro style that reminds people of the 1960s.
vocabulary.translation: 这家咖啡馆采用复古风格装修，让人想起20世纪60年代。

vocabulary.entry: vintage /ˈvɪntɪdʒ/ adj. 复古的；古着的
vocabulary.example: She likes to wear vintage dresses to stand out from the crowd.
vocabulary.translation: 她喜欢穿复古连衣裙，让自己在人群中脱颖而出。

vocabulary.entry: alternative /ɔːlˈtɜːnətɪv/ n. 可供选择的事物
vocabulary.example: We have to find an alternative solution to the problem as soon as possible.
vocabulary.translation: 我们必须尽快找到一个解决这个问题的替代方案。

vocabulary.entry: second-hand /ˌsekənd ˈhænd/ adj. 二手的；旧的
vocabulary.example: Buying second-hand furniture is a good way to save money.
vocabulary.translation: 购买二手家具是省钱的好办法。

vocabulary.entry: new lease of life /njuː liːs ɒv laɪf/ n. 新生；重焕生机
vocabulary.example: The old building was given a new lease of life after the renovation.
vocabulary.translation: 这座老建筑翻新后重焕了生机。

vocabulary.entry: rebrand /ˌriːˈbrænd/ v. 重塑品牌形象；更名
vocabulary.example: The company decided to rebrand its product to attract younger customers.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司决定为其产品重塑品牌形象，以吸引年轻顾客。

vocabulary.entry: trendy /ˈtrendi/ adj. 时髦的；流行的
vocabulary.example: That small boutique sells a lot of trendy accessories for young people.
vocabulary.translation: 那家小精品店售卖许多年轻人喜欢的时髦配饰。

vocabulary.entry: gingham-patterned /ˈɡɪŋəm ˈpætənd/ adj. 方格纹的
vocabulary.example: She bought a cute gingham-patterned skirt for the summer.
vocabulary.translation: 她买了一条可爱的方格纹短裙过夏天。

vocabulary.entry: jumble sale /ˈdʒʌmbl seɪl/ n. 旧货义卖活动
vocabulary.example: We donated some old books and clothes to the school jumble sale.
vocabulary.translation: 我们向学校的旧货义卖活动捐赠了一些旧书和旧衣服。

vocabulary.entry: boutique /buːˈtiːk/ n. 精品店
vocabulary.example: There is a fancy boutique selling handmade jewelry on this street.
vocabulary.translation: 这条街上有一家售卖手工珠宝的高档精品店。

vocabulary.entry: pop-up shop /ˈpɒp ʌp ʃɒp/ n. 快闪店
vocabulary.example: The brand opened a pop-up shop in the shopping mall for the holiday season.
vocabulary.translation: 该品牌假期期间在购物中心开了一家快闪店。

vocabulary.entry: circular economy /ˈsɜːkjələ ɪˈkɒnəmi/ n. 循环经济
vocabulary.example: Promoting a circular economy is crucial for sustainable development.
vocabulary.translation: 推动循环经济对可持续发展至关重要。

vocabulary.entry: prolong /prəˈlɒŋ/ v. 延长；拉长
vocabulary.example: Regular exercise can help prolong your life and improve your health.
vocabulary.translation: 规律运动有助于延长寿命，改善健康状况。

vocabulary.entry: manufacturing /ˌmænjuˈfæktʃərɪŋ/ n. 制造；生产
vocabulary.example: The manufacturing of this product requires a lot of skilled workers.
vocabulary.translation: 这款产品的生产需要大量熟练工人。

vocabulary.entry: Gen Z /ˌdʒen ˈzed/ n. Z世代
vocabulary.example: Gen Z are more concerned about environmental issues than previous generations.
vocabulary.translation: Z世代比前几代人更关注环境问题。

vocabulary.entry: kilo sale /ˈkiːləʊ seɪl/ n. 按公斤售卖的活动
vocabulary.example: We went to a vintage kilo sale and bought a bag of clothes for only £20.
vocabulary.translation: 我们去了一场复古服饰按公斤售卖的活动，只花20英镑就买了一袋衣服。

vocabulary.entry: upcycle /ˈʌpsaɪkl/ v. 升级改造（废旧物品）
vocabulary.example: She likes to upcycle old jeans into stylish tote bags.
vocabulary.translation: 她喜欢把旧牛仔裤升级改造成时髦的托特包。

vocabulary.entry: embroidery /ɪmˈbrɔɪdəri/ n. 刺绣；绣花工艺
vocabulary.example: The dress is decorated with beautiful floral embroidery on the collar.
vocabulary.translation: 这条连衣裙的领口处装饰着精美的花卉刺绣。

vocabulary.entry: patch /pætʃ/ n. 补丁；布贴
vocabulary.example: He sewed a colorful patch on the knee of his jeans to cover the hole.
vocabulary.translation: 他在牛仔裤的膝盖处缝了一块彩色补丁来遮盖破洞。

vocabulary.entry: addition /əˈdɪʃn/ n. 添加物；附加部分
vocabulary.example: The new addition to the building will be used as a meeting room.
vocabulary.translation: 这座建筑的新增部分将用作会议室。

vocabulary.entry: sustainability /səˌsteɪnəˈbɪləti/ n. 可持续性；能维持性
vocabulary.example: The sustainability of the fashion industry depends on reducing waste.
vocabulary.translation: 时尚行业的可持续性取决于减少浪费。

vocabulary.entry: buy into /baɪ ˈɪntuː/ v. 参与；认同并支持
vocabulary.example: More and more people are buying into the idea of green travel.
vocabulary.translation: 越来越多的人开始认同并支持绿色出行的理念。

sentences.chinese: 但这股潮流正在发生变化，复古服饰逐渐成为一种受欢迎且通常价格更低的选择。

sentences.chinese: 在英国，一家连锁超市还在部分门店推出了名为“珍爱复古批发”的二手服装品牌。

sentences.english: It’s also led to the rise of retro-fashion – items that your mum or dad wore decades ago that now look ‘cool’ again!
sentences.chinese: 这一趋势也带动了复古时尚的崛起——那些几十年前父母辈穿的衣服，如今又重新变得“时髦”起来！

sentences.english: It’s a big thing with younger people and has been helped by the rise of platforms like Depop and Vinted, which sell ‘worn’ clothes online.
sentences.chinese: 复古时尚在年轻人中十分流行，而Depop和Vinted这类线上二手服饰交易平台的兴起，也进一步推动了这股潮流。

sentences.chinese: 购买旧衣物的另一种流行方式是复古服饰按公斤售卖。

sentences.chinese: 人们挑选好想要的衣物后，按重量而非单件付费。

sentences.chinese: 但无论这些二手衣物是被直接穿着，还是经过重新设计，复古时尚的可持续性意味着它在未来一段时间内都会持续流行。
